                       October 31st.      37.

2.

Casualties from shells exploding in the
Western area.

At 10.10 a.m. 31/10/37 Inspector West telephoned to
the Station to the effect that shells had fallen in
Jessfield Park Camp and several of the Royal Ulster
Rifles had been wounded.

D.I. Toon attended and it was ascertained that at
about 9/55 a.m. 31/10/37 a shell had fallen on a hut
of the British Military Barracks, Jessfield Park and
the undermentioned members of the R.U.Rifles wounded.

L/C Dowey.
Rfle. McLacky.
"    Saunderson.

All suffered wounds in the legs, but Rfle Saunderson's
wounds were not of a serious nature.

During a visit re the above to the British Military
Hospital, Bubbling Well Road, it was learnt that
Rfle. Delaney who was admitted on 29/10/37 (see Diary 1 )
had died during the morning of 31/10/37 as a result of
his injuries.

Copy to:- D.C.(Divs).
          D.C.(Special Branch).

2.

西区炮弹爆炸造成的伤亡。

1937年10月31日上午10时10分，韦斯特（West）巡官致电警局，称兆丰公园营地落下炮弹，皇家阿尔斯特步枪团（Royal Ulster Rifles）数名士兵受伤。

探长图恩（Toon）前往处理，经查实，1937年10月31日上午约9时55分，一枚炮弹落在兆丰公园英军营房的一间棚屋上，导致下列皇家阿尔斯特步枪团成员受伤：

下士 多伊（Dowey）。
列兵 麦克拉克（McLacky）。
"     桑德森（Saunderson）。

所有人腿部均受创伤，但列兵桑德森的伤势并不严重。

在就上述事宜访问静安寺路英军医院期间，获悉于1937年10月29日入院（见日记1）的列兵德拉尼（Delaney），因伤重于1937年10月31日上午死亡。

抄送：- D.C.（各分区）。
          D.C.（特科）。

D. I.（分区督察）

Casualties from shells exploding in the
Western Area.

    During the shelling of Chinese positions
in the Western area by Japanese forces at about 5 p.m.
29/10/37 the undermentioned persons were injured in the
vicinity of Jessfield and Brenan Roads from shrapnel
and were conveyed to various hospitals by S.F.B.
Ambulance.
                    St. Luke's Hospital.
    (1) Sze Foo Chi. shrapnel wound on face.
    (2) Male Chinese, shrapnel wound on head. serious.
                St. Elizabeth's Hospital.
    (3) Koo Koo Sz. wound of scalp.
    (4) Kyung Tsai Di. wound of shoulder.
    (5) Kyung Kau Di, wound of thigh.

    Between 7 p.m. and 8 p.m. 29/10/37 the under-
mentioned persons were killed and wounded in Fah Wah
Village, East of Rockhill Avenue and about 100 yards
North of Avenue Haig when seven shells exploded in the
vicinity and were removed to St. Elizabeth's Hospital
by S.F.B. Ambulance.
    (6) Female Chinese(name unknown) killed.
    (7) Tsang Kyung Foh. fractured spine etc.
    (8) Tsang Zai Foh. Abrasion of nose.
    (9) Ts Kyung Mei. abrasion of scalp.

    During the shelling between 7 p.m. and 8 p.m.
29/10/37 the undermentioned persons were killed and
injured on Yu Yuen Road opposite Jessfield Park when a
shell exploded on the flower bed South of the Park,
shrapnel entering No's 1473, 1475 & 1477, Yu Yuen Road.

SHANGHAI TIMES - 31.10.37.

British Authorities In
Report On Affair Which
Took Lives Of Riflemen

STATEMENT ISSUED CLAIMS JAPANESE
ARMY WAS RESPONSIBLE; DENIAL
PUTS BLAME ON CHINESE

FUNERAL OF THREE MEN WILL OCCUR
AT BUBBLING WELL TO-MORROW

Many Residents Said Preparing To Leave Homes
In Western District; Repercussions In
Concession Are Said Very Slight

Having concluded an inquiry into the shelling of British posts and the area of the Western District near the perimeter on Friday night, the British authorities yesterday issued a statement to the effect that the unfortunate affair which resulted in the death of three soldiers and the wounding of two others was due to the action of the Japanese army.

The British authorities in Shanghai have also informed the Japanese that they are reporting to their Government the conclusion they have reached in the matter.

A formal statement dealing with the incident was issued here at a late hour yesterday afternoon through the British Consulate-General, this being presumably based on the findings of a military board of inquiry.

It was also stated that the Japanese Consul-General, Mr. Okamoto, accompanied by Admiral Honda, Naval Attache, Major-General Harada, Military Attache, and Mr. Okazaki, a Japanese Consul-General, called at the British Consulate-General yesterday and expressed their regrets to Admiral Sir Charles Little, Major-General A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett and Mr. Herbert Phillips, the Consul-General, for the occurrence.

The Japanese stated that a full report was being sent to their Government and that the investigation of the affair was still continuing.

Funeral To-morrow

In the meantime, it was announced that the funeral service for the late Rifleman Mellon, Rifleman Howard, and Rifleman O'Toole will take place at the Bubbling Well Cemetery at 3 o'clock to-morrow. An announcement released through the Royal Ulster Rifles here yesterday afternoon stated that it was not desired that the funeral should be of an official nature.

The condition of Riflemen McGuire and Delaney, both of whom were wounded on Friday night, was characterized as still serious yesterday. Both of these men are at the British Military Hospital suffering from several wounds sustained during the Jessfield shelling.

Different Viewpoints

Speaking during the course of a regular press conference yesterday, a Japanese naval spokesman denied that the shells were of Japanese origin, adding that they must have come from Chinese guns. It was claimed that the Japanese guns had not opened fire after sunset.

The Chinese answered these allegations during their press conference at a late hour yesterday afternoon. The Chinese spokesman stated, however, that he would rather leave the matter in the hands of the British authorities who were investigating.

In view of the possible danger to passengers, the China General Omnibus Company has discontinued its service to Jessfield Park. At the present time the buses are running only to Edinburgh Road, where they turn around and go back again.

Hardly calculated to ease the minds of residents on Yu Yuen Road beyond Edinburgh Road is the fact that no little activity is being carried on in the strengthening of redoubts in this neighbourhood. There is already one sturdy concrete redoubt on Yu Yuen Road, the strength of which would seem to indicate that the defence forces are not doing things by halves.

More Posts Built

A visit to the Jessfield area and the nearby British posts along the perimeter during the course of the afternoon yesterday revealed the fact that all had been quiet there after the tragic occurrences of the night before. A number of the shops in the vicinity were tightly closed, and the usual Saturday afternoon crowd was not to be found in the park.

At the junction of Brenan and Keswick Roads the troops there were putting up new and stronger sandbag positions some distance from the first line, possibly with the idea that if a temporary withdrawal from the railway became necessary these could be utilized.

A close check-up made here yesterday revealed the fact that very few residents in the western part of the French Concession are contemplating leaving their homes. A few residing close to the terminus of Avenue Joffre moved out during the shelling on Friday night, but the majority of these have since returned.

It is understood that the French authorities lodged no protest with regard to the two stray shells which landed in the Concession but are co-operating with the British in an investigation of the matter.

Company's Fast Work

The most important damage done in the Concession was to a telephone line near the I.S.S. Apartments, this having been torn asunder when struck by a shell. The telephone company got to work immediately to effect the necessary repairs and by 1.30 o'clock yesterday afternoon the 100 subscribers who had been deprived of their service were able to call up all their friends and tell what narrow escapes they had had.

That the telephone company has had its troubles elsewhere is evidenced by the fact that the Hungjao exchange has been completely evacuated. People having homes in the Hungjao area are able to keep in touch with their caretakers or servants in spite of the change, for the Lucerne exchange in Edinburgh Road is now handling these calls.

Many Packing Up

Somewhat alarmed by their experiences on the previous evening, many residents of the Western District were busily preparing to evacuate their homes yesterday, this being especially true of those residing along Columbia Road.

The more brave merely packed up their more valuable belongings and arranged things so they could be taken to a place of safety at a moment's notice. Those who decided to get out completely, however, were confronted with the more serious problem of finding a place to live.

Local rental agents received many applications for spaces during the course of the morning, but few were able to offer accommodations due to the fact that available apartments had already been rented in most instances. The evacuation of Hongkew went a long way toward creating a serious housing problem in Shanghai, and the latest developments have helped to aggravate the situation.

It is interesting to note that, contrary to the movement evidenced here toward the beginning of the hostilities, many of those who have left the Western District are seeking temporary accommodation in the Central District.

Shorter Bus Line

In the light of current developments, it is impossible to say what areas in the Western District are actually dangerous, but, generally speaking, the section which is bounded on the east by Columbia and Edinburgh Roads is being evacuated by a considerable number of residents. This does not mean that all people are leaving their homes, for even out on Yu Yuen Road as far as Jessfield Park many houses and apartments are still occupied.

《字林西报》 - 1937年10月31日。

英国当局
关于夺去步枪手生命事件的报告

发布的声明声称日本
军队负有责任；否认声明
将责任归咎于中国方面

三人葬礼将于明日
在静安寺举行

据说许多居民正准备离开
西区住所；据称租界内
反响甚微

英国当局在结束了对周五晚间英国哨位及西区周边地区遭受炮击的调查后，昨日发表声明称，导致三名士兵死亡、另外两名士兵受伤的这起不幸事件，是由日本军队的行动造成的。

上海英国当局还告知日方，他们正在向本国政府报告就此事项得出的结论。

昨天下午晚些时候，通过英国总领事馆在此发布了一份关于该事件的正式声明，这大概是基于军事调查委员会的调查结果。

声明还称，日本总领事冈本先生（Mr. Okamoto）在海軍武官本田海军少将（Admiral Honda）、陆军武官原田陆军少将（Major-General Harada）以及日本总领事冈崎先生（Mr. Okazaki）的陪同下，于昨日拜访了英国总领事馆，并向查尔斯·利特尔海军上将爵士（Admiral Sir Charles Little）、A. P. D. 泰尔弗-斯莫利特陆军少将（Major-General A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett）和总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯先生（Mr. Herbert Phillips）对发生此事表示遗憾。

日方表示，一份完整报告正发送至其政府，且对该事件的调查仍在继续。

明日葬礼

与此同时，官方宣布，已故列兵梅隆、列兵霍华德和列兵奥图尔的葬礼将于明天下午3点在静安寺公墓举行。昨天下午皇家阿尔斯特步枪团在此发布的一份公告称，不希望葬礼具有官方性质。

昨晚周五受伤的两名列兵麦奎尔和德拉尼的状况，昨天仍被描述为严重。这两人都在英军医院，因在兆丰公园炮击中遭受的多处创伤而接受治疗。

不同观点

一位日本海军发言人在昨天的例行记者会上发言时，否认炮弹来自日本方面，并补充说它们肯定来自中国火炮。声称日军火炮在日落后并未开火。

中方在昨天下午晚些时候举行的记者会上对这些指控作出了回应。然而，中方发言人表示，他宁愿将此事项留给正在调查的英国当局处理。

鉴于乘客可能面临的危险，华商公共汽车公司已停止前往兆丰公园的服务。目前，公共汽车仅运行至爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road），在那里掉头返回。

让爱丁堡路以外愚园路居民的安心程度大打折扣的事实是，该地区的碉堡加固工作正在进行中，活动不少。愚园路上已经有一座坚固的混凝土碉堡，其强度似乎表明防御部队做事并不半途而废。

修建更多哨位

昨天下午对兆丰公园地区及沿周边附近的英国哨位的走访显示，在前一夜的悲剧发生后，那里一直平静无事。附近的许多商店紧紧关闭，公园里也没有往常周六下午的人群。

在布伦南路和凯斯威克路（Keswick Road）的交汇处，那里的部队正在距离第一线一定距离的地方构筑新的、更坚固的沙袋阵地，可能是考虑到如果暂时从铁路线撤退，这些阵地可以被利用。

昨天在此进行的仔细核查显示，法租界西部很少有居民打算离开家园。少数居住在霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）终点站附近的居民在周五晚上的炮击期间搬离，但其中大多数人此后已返回。

据悉，法国当局并未就落入租界的两枚流弹提出抗议，但正与英国方面合作调查此事。

公司的高效工作

租界内最严重的损坏发生在国际储蓄会公寓（I.S.S. Apartments）附近的一条电话线上，该线路被炮弹击中后断裂。电话公司立即着手进行必要的维修，到昨天下午1点30分，100名失去服务的用户已能够打电话给所有朋友，讲述他们的死里逃生经历。

电话公司在其他地方也遇到了麻烦，虹桥交换局已完全撤离便是明证。尽管发生了这一变化，家在虹桥地区的人们仍能与其看守人或仆人保持联系，因为现在爱丁堡路的卢塞恩（Lucerne）交换局正在处理这些呼叫。

许多人打包行李

由于前一天晚上的经历令人心有余悸，西区的许多居民昨天正忙着准备撤离家园，哥伦比亚路（Columbia Road）沿线的居民尤其如此。

较为勇敢的人只是打包了更贵重的物品，并安排妥当，以便在接到通知的瞬间就能转移到安全地带。然而，那些决定彻底搬离的人则面临着寻找住处的更严峻问题。

当地租赁代理商在上午接到了许多租房申请，但由于可用公寓在大多数情况下已被租出，很少有人能提供住宿。虹口的撤离在很大程度上造成了上海严重的住房问题，而最新的事态发展加剧了这一局面。

值得注意的是，与敌对行动开始时这里显现出的动向相反，许多离开西区的人正在中区寻求临时住所。

缩短的公交线路

鉴于当前事态，很难说西区哪些地区实际上处于危险之中，但一般而言，东以哥伦比亚路和爱丁堡路为界的区域正有大量居民撤离。这并不意味着所有人都要离开家园，因为即使在远至兆丰公园的愚园路上，许多房屋和公寓仍有人居住。

CHINA PRESS - 31.10.37.

British Blame
Nippon Shells
In Death Of 3

An official statement, dispelling all doubt as to the Japanese origin of the shells which killed Rifleman Joseph O'Toole at the Honeyland Cafe on Yu Yuen Road, and caused the death of Rifleman James Mellon and Rifleman William Christopher Howard at Post J2 on Friday evening, was issued by H.M. British Consulate-General yesterday.

The statement announces that the British authorities here have informed the Japanese authorities that they consider the shelling of British posts and the area of the Western district near the perimeter which occurred on the evening of October 29, resulting in the death of three British soldiers and the wounding of two others, as due to the action of the Japanese Army. The British authorities, continued the statement, are reporting to the British Government in this sense.

It was further stated that the Japanese Consul-General, Mr. S. Okamoto, accompanied by Admiral Honda, Naval Attache, Major-General Harada, Military Attache, and Mr. Okazaki, a Japanese Consul-General, called at the British Consulate-General yesterday. Mr. Okamoto expressed his regrets to Admiral Sir Charles Little, Major-General A.P.D. Telfer-Smollett, and Mr. Herbert Phillips, Consul-General, over the occurrence. He said that a full report was being sent to the Japanese Government and that their investigation of the affair was still continuing.

The opinion of many military observers here, who are aware of the exact positions of the Japanese batteries, informed a representative of THE CHINA PRESS yesterday that if the shelling of the British perimeter was accidental, then a serious threat to the Settlement existed because of unbelievably poor marksmanship on the part of the Japanese. It was pointed out that if the Japanese were shelling Chinese positions at the time, then their aim was no less, and possibly more, than 20 degrees off the mark.

Foreign military experts here said yesterday that if an unmolested artillery unit can possibly fire 20 degrees off its mark, then the men comprising the squad should be trusted with nothing more deadly than a pop-gun.

Chinese Fleet Nippon Report
The Japanese allegation that the shells were fired by the Chinese forces with a view to estranging the relations between foreign powers and Japan was "as ridiculous as it was blatant," declared a Chinese military spokesman last night.

A Chinese high commander told him, the spokesman continued, that these shells were not fired from Chinese guns and that he had every reason to believe that the British military authorities examining the matter would arrive at a fair and just conclusion as to their origin.

《字林西报》 - 1937年10月31日。

英国方面指责
日军炮弹
致三人死亡

英国驻上海总领事馆昨日发表正式声明，消除了所有疑虑，确认在愚园路“蜜地咖啡馆”（Honeyland Cafe）炸死步枪兵约瑟夫·奥图尔（Joseph O'Toole），并于周五晚间在J2哨所导致步枪兵詹姆斯·梅隆（James Mellon）和步枪兵威廉·克里斯托弗·霍华德（William Christopher Howard）死亡的炮弹系来自日本方面。

该声明宣布，驻沪英国当局已告知日本当局，他们认为10月29日晚发生的对英国哨所及西区周边区域的炮击事件——该事件导致三名英国士兵死亡，另两人受伤——系日本陆军所为。声明接着称，英国当局正就此向英国政府报告。

声明还指出，日本总领事冈本先生（Mr. S. Okamoto）在日本海军武官本田海军上将（Admiral Honda）、日本陆军武官原田少将（Major-General Harada）以及日本总领事冈崎先生（Mr. Okazaki）的陪同下，于昨日拜访了英国总领事馆。冈本先生就此事向英国皇家海军中将查尔斯·利特尔爵士（Sir Charles Little）、A.P.D. 泰尔弗-斯莫利特少将（Major-General A.P.D. Telfer-Smollett）以及总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯先生（Mr. Herbert Phillips）表示遗憾。他说，一份详尽的报告正送往日本政府，且他们对该事件的调查仍在继续。

许多了解日军炮兵确切位置的军事观察员昨日向《字林西报》记者表示，如果此次对英国防区周边的炮击是意外，那么由于日军准头差得令人难以置信，租界面临着严重威胁。有人指出，如果当时日军是在炮击中国军队阵地，那么他们的瞄准偏差至少，甚至可能超过20度。

驻沪外国军事专家昨日表示，如果一支未受干扰的炮兵部队竟然能偏离目标20度射击，那么组成该小队的士兵除了玩具枪之外，不应被信任使用任何更具致命性的武器。

中国舰队驳斥日方报道
一名中国军方发言人昨晚宣称，日方声称炮弹由中国军队发射、旨在疏远列强与日本关系的说法“既荒谬又露骨”。

该发言人继续说，一位中国高级指挥官告诉他，这些炮弹并非由中国火炮发射，他有充分理由相信，正在调查此事的英国军事当局将就其来源得出公平和公正的结论。

CHINA PRESS - 30.10.37.

**3 Ulster Riflemen Killed, Wounded When Shell Explodes In Jessfield Sector Outpost**

**Missile Of Death Lands In Midst Of Group Drinking Tea**

**2 CHINESE DIE, 7 HURT ON AVE. HAIG**

**Shell On Jessfield Road Believed Of Japanese Origin**

Three British soldiers were killed and three others were wounded, two seriously, when more than 15 shells believed to have been fired from Japanese artillery north of Soochow Creek, landed and exploded in the Jessfield Park area shortly before 8 o'clock last night.

The dead and wounded are all members of the Royal Ulster Rifles who are manning the boundary defenses of the western district of the International Settlement.

The dead are:
Rifleman James Mellon, age 24, of Londonderry, Ireland, multiple shrapnel wounds.
Rifleman William Christopher Howard, age 26, of Coochram, Ireland, multiple shrapnel wounds.
Rifleman Patrick Joseph O'Toole, age 23, of Dublin, shrapnel wounds to the head.

The wounded are:
Rifleman Jack McGuire, of Strabane, Tyrone, Ireland, multiple shrapnel wounds.
Rifleman Robert Delaney, of Belfast, Ireland, serious wounds about the body.
Rifleman Campbell, also a native of Ireland, only slight wounds.

**May Lose Leg**

Riflemen McGuire and Delaney are now in the British Military Hospital. Their conditions are considered grave and operations were performed on both last night. Delaney may lose one leg and McGuire a foot.

Mellon and Howard were killed outright when a shell made a direct hit on the British dugout near the Jessfield Railway Bridge. The time was 7.35 p.m. The British outpost unit was at the time gathered around a small camp fire drinking "mugs" of tea and having a light meal.

A CHINA PRESS representative who visited the outpost late last night saw the blood-splattered helmets of the two dead Ulsters within about two feet of where the shell hit the sandbagged side of the outpost. Their white tea "mugs," also blood-smeared, were left on the spot where their owners had fallen but a few hours before.

Comrades of the wounded and killed Ulsters were visibly moved by the deaths within their ranks. Men at various posts asked eager questions of newspapermen who visited the area, saying that they had not been informed other than by rumor of what had actually occurred.

There were only seven men in the post at the time and but one, Rifleman Tomlanson, escaped unscathed. McGuire, Delaney and Campbell were all wounded at this point.

Rifleman O'Toole was killed while he was seated in the Honeyland Cafe at 1475 Yu Yuen Road just across the street from the Jessfield Park entrance. Three shells landed in a grass street island between the park entrance and the cafe and all exploded with terrific detonations.

**Died Almost Instantly**

Shrapnel shattered the windows of the cafe, wounding O'Toole about the head. He died almost immediately. The time of this incident was 7.50 p.m. A Chinese waitress employed in the place, known as "Mabel" to the Tommies who patronize the establishment, was cut about the arm by flying glass. Two Chinese, a man and a woman, outside the cafe and believed to have been refugees, were both killed. Several other Chinese were reported to have been wounded but the exact number could not be determined. Several hundred refugees were on the road at the time.

A British police officer, riding a motorcycle along the street not far from the spot where the shells fell, had a narrow escape from electrocution.

Overhead trolley wires were blasted down as a result of the explosions and they fell on the officer's motorcycle. The resulting shock threw him from his seat. He stated last night that he was saved from death by the rubber grips on the handle-bars of his machine.

Riflemen Mellon and Howard were killed by the same shell which scored a direct hit on Post J2 behind the Jessfield Park Zoo at 7:50 p.m.

**Due To Leave For Home**

Rifleman Mellon was due to leave for England, with the party of nearly 300 men from the Ulster Rifles, whose term of service was to expire within six months.

Last night's three deaths brings the total of men of this regiment killed by Japanese fire to four within six days, Rifleman McGowan having been butchered by the machine-gun fire of a Japanese plane last Sunday on Keswick Road.

The shelling last night was an artillery duel between Chinese and Japanese positions. Just who started it is not known. At any rate, the Jessfield zone was showered with short range shells and for almost an hour the place was in a near panic. More than 200 Chinese refugees were in the zone and panic-stricken, and all scrambled for cover. The entrance to Jessfield Park was badly damaged while it was reported that several shells landed in the park itself.

After the death of the three soldiers, British military officials communicated with both Chinese and Japanese headquarters asking them to stop shelling. The two sides were informed that enough damage had been done for the evening. The shelling shortly afterwards stopped.

**Returned, Repaired Post**

Despite the fact that their dugout had been shattered, men of the Royal Ulster Rifles went back to the post, repaired it and were still there early this morning, manning the defense as usual.

While the British headquarters would make no statement as to the identity of the shells, private opinions expressed by foreign observers were to the effect that they were Japanese. The bursting shells threw the shrapnel to the south, indicating that they had come from the north.

Jessfield was not the only area in the western district which suffered as a result of shelling last night. One shell fell in a small Chinese settlement just off Avenue Haig and killed two Chinese, wounding seven others. Three other shells fell on an open lot off Route Camille Loriot not far from Columbia Circle and although they all exploded, there were no casualties. Another shell is said to have fallen near the end of Avenue Joffre, causing no casualties.

《字林西报》 - 1937年10月30日。

**杰斯菲尔德区哨所内炮弹爆炸，三名阿尔斯特步枪兵死伤**

**夺命飞弹落在饮茶人群中间**

**海格路两名中国人死亡，七人受伤**

**杰斯菲尔德路炮弹被认为系日军所为**

昨晚8点前不久，据信由苏州河北岸日军火炮发射的15多发炮弹落入并爆炸于杰斯菲尔德公园（Jessfield Park）区域，造成三名英国士兵死亡，另三人受伤，其中两人伤势严重。

死伤者均为皇家阿尔斯特步枪团（Royal Ulster Rifles）成员，该团负责防守国际公共租界西区的边界防线。

死者如下：
步枪兵詹姆斯·梅隆（James Mellon），24岁，爱尔兰伦敦德里人，多处弹片伤。
步枪兵威廉·克里斯托弗·霍华德（William Christopher Howard），26岁，爱尔兰库克拉姆（Coochram）人，多处弹片伤。
步枪兵帕特里克·约瑟夫·奥图尔（Patrick Joseph O'Toole），23岁，都柏林人，头部弹片伤。

伤者如下：
步枪兵杰克·麦圭尔（Jack McGuire），爱尔兰蒂龙郡斯特拉班（Strabane, Tyrone）人，多处弹片伤。
步枪兵罗伯特·德莱尼（Robert Delaney），爱尔兰贝尔法斯特人，身体多处重伤。
步枪兵坎贝尔（Campbell），亦为爱尔兰人，仅受轻伤。

**可能截肢**

步枪兵麦圭尔和德莱尼现均在英军医院。他们的病情被认为危重，昨晚两人都接受了手术。德莱尼可能失去一条腿，麦圭尔可能失去一只脚。

梅隆和霍华德在一枚炮弹直接击中杰斯菲尔德铁路桥附近的英军掩体时当场身亡。时间是晚上7点35分。当时，该英军前哨单位的士兵正围着一小堆营火，喝着“大杯”茶，吃着简餐。

《字林西报》记者深夜探访该哨所时，看到两名死去的阿尔斯特士兵血迹斑斑的头盔，就在炮弹击中哨所沙袋侧壁处附近约两英尺的地方。他们白色的茶杯也沾满了血迹，留在几小时前主人倒下的地方。

死伤阿尔斯特士兵的战友们对队伍中的伤亡明显感到悲痛。各哨位的士兵急切地向到访的记者询问情况，称除了谣言外，他们并未获知实际发生的情况。

当时哨所内只有七人，只有一人，即步枪兵汤姆林森（Tomlanson），毫发无损。麦圭尔、德莱尼和坎贝尔均在此处受伤。

步枪兵奥图尔是在坐在愚园路1475号“蜜地咖啡馆”内时身亡的，该咖啡馆就在杰斯菲尔德公园入口马路对面。三枚炮弹落在公园入口与咖啡馆之间的草地街心岛上，全部剧烈爆炸。

**几乎瞬间死亡**

弹片震碎了咖啡馆的窗户，奥图尔头部受伤。他几乎立即死亡。此事发生的时间是晚上7点50分。在该店工作的一名中国女服务员，被光顾此店的英国士兵称为“梅布尔”（Mabel），被飞溅的玻璃割伤了手臂。咖啡馆外的两名中国人，一男一女，据信是难民，均被炸死。据报道还有其他几名中国人受伤，但确切人数无法确定。当时路上有数百名难民。

一名英国警官骑着摩托车沿街道行驶，距离炮弹落点不远，险些触电身亡。

架空电车线因爆炸被炸断，掉落在该警官的摩托车上。由此产生的电击将他从座位上甩下。他昨晚表示，是摩托车把手上的橡胶握把救了他一命。

步枪兵梅隆和霍华德是被同一枚炮弹炸死的，该炮弹于晚上7点50分直接击中了杰斯菲尔德公园动物园后面的J2哨所。

**原定回国**

步枪兵梅隆原定随近300名服役期将在六个月内届满的阿尔斯特步枪团成员一起返回英国。

昨晚的三起死亡事件使该团在六天内死于日军火力的人数达到四人，此前步枪兵麦高恩（McGowan）上周日在基威克路（Keswick Road）被一架日本飞机的机枪扫射致死。

昨晚的炮击是中日双方阵地间的炮战。究竟是谁先开炮尚不清楚。无论如何，杰斯菲尔德区遭到了短程炮弹的密集轰击，该地区在将近一小时内处于近乎恐慌的状态。区内有200多名中国难民，惊慌失措，纷纷寻找掩护。杰斯菲尔德公园入口受损严重，另有报道称几枚炮弹落在了公园内部。

在三名士兵死亡后，英国军事官员与中国和日本司令部取得联系，要求他们停止炮击。双方被告知，当晚造成的破坏已经够多了。炮击随后不久便停止了。

**返回并修复哨所**

尽管掩体已被炸毁，皇家阿尔斯特步枪团的士兵们还是回到了哨所，进行了修复，并于今日清晨仍在那里，像往常一样执行防御任务。

虽然英国司令部未就炮弹的来源发表声明，但外国观察人士私下表达的意见认为它们是日军的。爆炸的炮弹将弹片向南抛射，表明炮弹来自北方。

杰斯菲尔德并非昨晚因炮击而遭受损失的西区唯一区域。一枚炮弹落在海格路（Avenue Haig）附近的一个小型中国居民区，炸死两名中国人，炸伤另外七人。另外三枚炮弹落在离哥伦比亚圈（Columbia Circle）不远的卡米耶·洛里奥路（Route Camille Loriot）旁的一块空地上，虽然全部爆炸，但未造成伤亡。据称还有一枚炮弹落在霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）尽头附近，未造成伤亡。

SHANGHAI TIMES - 30.10.37.

THREE ULSTER RIFLEMEN
KILLED AT JESSFIELD

Shrapnel, Bullets And
Shells Create Reign Of
Terror Among Civilians

TWO "TOMMIES" SERIOUSLY WOUNDED
AS GUNFIRE FROM NORTH RAKES
BOUNDARY OF SETTLEMENT

MISSILES FALL ON STREETS AND HOUSES
ON EDGE OF WHOLE WEST EXTENSION

Special Precautions Taken By Police; Roads To
Danger Zone Closed; Many Residents Isolated
By Hit Near Pichon Telephone Exchange

Three men of the Royal Ulster Rifles were killed and two seriously wounded last night as a reign of terror descended on the western extension area of the Settlement to the accompani-ment of the whine of shells, shrapnel and bullets which raked the edge of a district almost totally occupied by foreign residents.

Between 6 and 8.30 p.m., when the barrage from the north was at its height, a veritable hail of death poured from the skies, shells exploding in streets and on houses within the Settlement and Concession and along the defence front held by the British forces.

Forewarned by British Military and Consular authorities, civilian occupants of the area were nevertheless stricken by the swiftness with which the attack fell and took cover in whatever protection was offered by their homes. Immediately the barrage ceased, however, there was a gradual movement out of the dis-trict, most of the evacuees shifting out with only their immediate necessities.

So far as could be ascertained last night, no foreign civilian casualties had been sustained, but a number of foreign residences were struck by shells with varying damage.

Five Chinese were reported killed, including a woman and an infant and many more were injured, by shell, shrapnel and stray bullets that rained all over the western area, right into the French Concession.

Three Killed

The following three men of the Royal Ulster Rifles, at present man-ning the western area perimeter, Sector D, were killed:

Rifleman Joseph O'Toole, 23, native of Dublin, killed in the Honeyland Cafe on Yu Yuen Road.

Rifleman James Mellon, 24, na-tive of Londonderry, killed in Post J2.

Rifleman William Christopher Howard, 26, native of Dublin, killed in Post J2.

Two Wounded

The following two riflemen were seriously injured in addition to five others, who were slightly hurt:

Rifleman Jack McGuire, 25, na-tive of Strabane, County Tyrone.

Rifleman Robert Delaney, 24, native of Belfast.

Indication that all kinds of miss-iles were likely to fall all over the Western Area were seen early in the afternoon when trench mortars, light field pieces, machine-guns and rifles were brought into action by both sides. Shrapnel exploded in the air, not many yards over the railway line, while British troops took cover and the Chinese con-tinued to dig trenches, using rails as uprights.

No Statement

No statement on the casualties was issued by the British Military authorities last night. It is under-stood, however, that an inquiry has been launched immediately under the direction of Major-General A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett, Commanding the British Forces in Shanghai, and as soon as it is ascertained by which of the two warring forces the shells were fired an official protest will be lodged.

It was intimated in foreign mili-tary circles last night that nothing, but unthinkably poor marksman-ship could have caused the shells to have fallen within the British sector.

Rifleman O'Toole, was the first to be killed, when a shell landed in the Honeyland Cafe, opposite Jess-field Park, at about 6.45 p.m. At the time there was a group of refugees outside, three of them being killed and eight others wounded. Rifleman O'Toole was conveyed to the Coun-try Hospital in, a Shanghai Fire Brigade Emergency Ambulance, but was pronounced dead on arrival.

Riflemen Mellon and Howard were killed at Post J2, where Riflemen

Guire and DeLaney were injured. Three other men sustained slight injuries.

No Phone Service

Added to the discomfort of sleep-ing under a barrage of shells and rifle fire, numerous residents of the western district were further handicapped when their telephone service was disrupted. The Shang-hai Telephone Company reported last night that several of their cables were broken down in the Route Pichon Exchange area. About a hundred lines, all numbering from 20,000 were affected, the service being disrupted at about 7 o'clock.

Numerous residents of Columbia Circle and the far end of Great West-ern Road had moved away from their homes before the deadly barrage descended on the city, while others collected only the most necessary belongings after the firing had quieted down a little and moved further into the Settlement for the night, where they may perhaps have to spend considerable time before being able once more to return to their form-er abodes. Residents along Yu Yuen Road, not far from Jessfield Park, also moved, as did a number residing in the western section of the French Concession. However, no general exodus of foreigners was witnessed last night.

Taking all precautionary meas-ures Settlement Police last night stopped all traffic proceeding west of Jessfield Park along Yu Yuen Road. Prior to the evening no one was allowed west of Keswick Road.

Many Missiles

Apart from the shells that account-ed for the casualties among the Royal Ulster Rifles, three other shells fell in the British sector about 50 yards west of Avenue Haig, near the end of Avenue Joffre. One of these exploded in a small Chinese settlement killing one woman and an infant and wounding seven others. At about the same time two other shells exploded on a vacant plot of ground off Rue Camille Loriot-but no one was injured here. The homes of Mr. A. J. Hughes at 415 Great Western Road and Mr. D. G. Mirams, Court 10, 410 Great Western Road were struck by shrapnel. Mr. Hughes is a former member of the Council, and a well known member of the British com-munity, while Mr. Mirams is con-nected with the Public Works De-partment.

Mrs. Hughes and children were in the house at the time, but fortun-ately were not injured.

The Shanghai German newspaper, the "Ostasiatischer Lloyd," will not appear this morning owing to its office being in the western danger zone, wherein the power has been cut off.

《上海泰晤士报》- 1937年10月30日。

三名阿尔斯特步枪团士兵
在兆丰公园附近丧生

弹片、子弹和炮弹
在平民中制造恐怖统治

两名“英国兵”受重伤
来自北面的枪火扫射
租界边界

投掷物落在整个西区扩展部
边缘的街道和房屋上

警方采取特别预防措施；通往
危险区的道路被封闭；许多居民因
毕勋路电话交换局附近的袭击而受困

昨晚，随着炮弹、弹片和子弹的呼啸声席卷了几乎完全由外籍居民占据的地区边缘，恐怖统治降临租界西区扩展部，皇家阿尔斯特步枪团（Royal Ulster Rifles）的三名士兵丧生，两人受重伤。

下午6点至8点30分之间，当来自北面的炮击达到高潮时，真正的死亡冰雹从天而降，炮弹在租界和法租界的街道和房屋内爆炸，并沿着英军坚守的防御前线爆炸。

尽管事先得到了英国军方和领事当局的通知，该地区的平民居住者仍因袭击来得如此迅速而受到打击，并在家中寻找任何可用的掩护。然而，炮击一停止，人们便开始逐渐撤离该地区，大多数撤离者仅携带生活必需品。

据昨晚查明，没有外籍平民伤亡，但一些外籍住宅被炮弹击中，受损程度不一。

据报道，有五名中国人死亡，其中包括一名妇女和一名婴儿，还有更多人被遍布西区、直落法租界的炮弹、弹片和流弹所伤。

三人死亡

以下三名目前驻守西区外围D防区的皇家阿尔斯特步枪团士兵丧生：

步枪兵约瑟夫·奥图尔（Joseph O'Toole），23岁，都柏林人，在愚园路蜜兰咖啡馆（Honeyland Cafe）丧生。

步枪兵詹姆斯·梅隆（James Mellon），24岁，伦敦德里人，在J2哨所丧生。

步枪兵威廉·克里斯托弗·霍华德（William Christopher Howard），26岁，都柏林人，在J2哨所丧生。

两人受伤

除另有五人受轻伤外，以下两名步枪兵受重伤：

步枪兵杰克·麦圭尔（Jack McGuire），25岁，蒂龙郡斯特拉班（Strabane）人。

步枪兵罗伯特·德莱尼（Robert Delaney），24岁，贝尔法斯特人。

当天下午早些时候，双方投入了战壕迫击炮、轻型野战炮、机枪和步枪，这表明各种投掷物可能会落在西区的各个地方。弹片在离铁路线仅几码的空中爆炸，英军士兵寻找掩护，而中国军队则继续挖掘战壕，利用铁轨作为支柱。

无声明

英国军方当局昨晚未就伤亡情况发表声明。然而，据悉，驻沪英军司令A. P. D. 特尔弗-斯莫利特（A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett）少将已立即展开调查，一旦查明炮弹是由交战双方中的哪一方发射的，将提出正式抗议。

昨晚外籍军事界人士暗示，只有难以想象的糟糕射击技术才会导致炮弹落入英军防区。

奥图尔步枪兵是第一个丧生的，当时一枚炮弹在下午6点45分左右落在兆丰公园对面的蜜兰咖啡馆。当时外面有一群难民，其中三人死亡，另外八人受伤。奥图尔步枪兵由上海救火会紧急救护车送往宏恩医院（Country Hospital），但抵达时被宣布死亡。

梅隆和霍华德步枪兵在J2哨所丧生，麦圭尔和德莱尼步枪兵在该处受伤。另有三人受轻伤。

电话服务中断

除了在炮弹和步枪火力下睡觉的不适之外，西区许多居民的电话服务中断，使他们的处境更加困难。上海电话公司昨晚报告称，其在毕勋路（Route Pichon）交换局区域的几条电缆被切断。大约一百条线路受到影响，所有号码均以20,000开头，服务在7点左右中断。

在致命的炮击降临城市之前，哥伦比亚圈（Columbia Circle）和大西路（Great Western Road）远端的许多居民已经搬离家园，而其他人则在枪声稍息后仅收集最必要的物品，并搬入租界深处过夜，他们可能不得不在那里度过相当长的时间，才能再次返回以前的住所。愚园路沿线、距兆丰公园不远的居民也进行了搬迁，法租界西部的一些居民也是如此。然而，昨晚并未出现外籍人士大规模撤离的现象。

采取一切预防措施，租界警察昨晚封锁了沿愚园路向西经过兆丰公园的所有交通。傍晚之前，任何人不得进入凯斯威克路（Keswick Road）以西地区。

大量投掷物

除了造成皇家阿尔斯特步枪团伤亡的炮弹外，另有三枚炮弹落在英军防区，位于海格路（Avenue Haig）以西约50码处，靠近霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）尽头。其中一枚在一个小型华人聚居区爆炸，造成一名妇女和一名婴儿死亡，另有七人受伤。大约在同一时间，另外两枚炮弹在卡米耶·洛里奥路（Rue Camille Loriot）旁的一块空地上爆炸——但此处无人受伤。一枚炮弹落在福开森路（Route Ferguson）以西150码处，另一枚落在路中间，离法国人雷蒙先生（Mr. Remond）居住的房子不远。一块窗玻璃被碎片击碎。

大西路415号A. J. 休斯先生（Mr. A. J. Hughes）和大西路410号10号院D. G. 米拉姆斯先生（Mr. D. G. Mirams）的住宅被弹片击中。休斯先生是前工部局董事，也是英国社区中的知名人士，而米拉姆斯先生与工务处有关联。

休斯夫人和孩子当时在屋内，但幸运的是未受伤。

上海德文报纸《东亚劳埃德报》（Ostasiatischer Lloyd）今晨停刊，因其办公室位于西部危险区，电力已被切断。
